sentences.text: There are some exemptions to know.
A vessel under seven meters at anchor, when not in or near a narrow channel, fairway or anchorage, or where other vessels normally navigate, doesn’t need anchor lights or a shape.
A vessel under twelve meters aground doesn’t need the aground lights or shapes.
Inland, a vessel under twenty meters at anchor in a special anchorage area designated by the Coast Guard doesn’t need anchor lights or a shape.
Finally, Rule thirty-one says that where a seaplane or wing-in-ground craft can’t show lights and shapes exactly as required, she shows lights and shapes as closely similar as possible.
